I've written the mapper at `out/transform.ts`. It type-checks with `sh in/harness/check.sh` and gives sensible rows for both sample patients. I also ran a scratch test (`out/scratch.test.ts`) on cases the samples don't show. It covered mmol/L readings, a HI reading, a typed copy of a cuff reading, a superseded day page and a retracted one. It also covered a stopped med and a held med, a brand-only typed name, a range dose, a time-scope cut at the Chicago midnight boundary, and junk items. Every case came out as I intended.

The judgment calls:

- **Which items count:** an item counts if its `recorded` time falls on or before `asOf` in Chicago time. A retracted item's own `supersedes` and `retracts` are ignored, so it can't hide anything. The medication list is the latest current My Medicines save. Day pages are all current ones, but if two are current for the same date, the newest wins, since the schema says a new page restates the whole day.
- **Ingredient:** a picked search result wins over the typed name. I parse its display text, drop the salt ("rosuvastatin calcium" becomes "rosuvastatin") and translate brands. `rxnorm_ingredient` is set only when the display is a plain ingredient. Product codes and salt-form codes ("metformin hydrochloride") don't count. A typed name gets an ingredient only if it matches a built-in brand or generic list. Otherwise, as with "water pill" or "m_61", it is left blank.
- **Dose:** a direction with no count ("morning") means one tablet, converted to mass when the strength is known. Ranges ("1 or 2"), puffs, liquid concentrations and sliding scales get no dose. If the typed strength and the picked product's strength differ by exactly 1000 (a mg/mcg slip), I use the product's strength. That is how both sample patients' levothyroxine "75 mg" comes out as 75 mcg. Any other disagreement leaves the dose blank.
- **Status from the free-text note:**
  - A medicine marked `taking`, or `stopped`, whose note says "for now", "on hold", "paused", "until…" or "restart" becomes `held`.
  - `stop_reason` is set only when the note clearly matches a reason (side effect, switched, didn't work, and so on). Otherwise it is left out, and the note goes in `status_reason_text`.
  - `status_since` is the patient's own `started` or `stopped` date at its given precision. I don't fill it from the save date.
- **Vitals:** times are reported exactly as written on the phone. Glucose is read in each reading's own unit and converted at 18.016, so HI/LO limits come out as 600 and 20 mg/dL. A typed reading with the same values as a device reading within 5 minutes is dropped, keeping the device copy. Clearly bad typed values (e.g. a typed 510/90) are still reported, because the mapper must not correct the source.
- **Left empty:** problems, allergies and labs. HomeLog has no such lists, and I chose not to build allergy rows from free-text stop notes. Dose logs and diary notes produce no rows.
- **Sensitivity:** a small built-in list of clearly sensitive drugs (antidepressants and antipsychotics, addiction treatment, contraceptives, HIV drugs) gets a sensitivity category. HomeLog itself marks nothing as sensitive.

The weakest spots are the keyword rules for `held` and stop reasons, and the fixed name lists. Notes worded in ways I didn't anticipate, or brands not on the list, will be misread or left blank.
